# Finding ∫ -3x⁴sin(x) dx

## Setting Up Integration by Parts (Tabular Method)

I'll factor out the constant: **-3** ∫ x⁴ sin(x) dx

Using the **tabular method** for ∫ x⁴ sin(x) dx:

| Sign | Differentiate x⁴ | Integrate sin(x) |
|------|-----------------|-----------------|
| +    | x⁴              | -cos(x)         |
| −    | 4x³             | -sin(x)         |
| +    | 12x²            | cos(x)          |
| −    | 24x             | sin(x)          |
| +    | 24              | -cos(x)         |
| −    | 0               | -sin(x)         |

## Combining Terms

$$\int x^4 \sin(x)\,dx = -x^4\cos(x) + 4x^3\sin(x) + 12x^2\cos(x) - 24x\sin(x) - 24\cos(x)$$

## Multiplying by -3

$$\int -3x^4\sin(x)\,dx = 3x^4\cos(x) - 12x^3\sin(x) - 36x^2\cos(x) + 72x\sin(x) + 72\cos(x) + C$$

## Verification

Differentiating the result:
- d/dx[3x⁴cos(x)] = 12x³cos(x) − 3x⁴sin(x)
- d/dx[−12x³sin(x)] = −36x²sin(x) − 12x³cos(x)
- d/dx[−36x²cos(x)] = −72xcos(x) + 36x²sin(x)
- d/dx[72xsin(x)] = 72sin(x) + 72xcos(x)
- d/dx[72cos(x)] = −72sin(x)

All terms cancel except **−3x⁴sin(x)** ✓

<answer>3*x**4*cos(x) - 12*x**3*sin(x) - 36*x**2*cos(x) + 72*x*sin(x) + 72*cos(x) + C</answer>
